comments.author: crabmusket
comments.story: 99 Bottles of OOP now available in Python
comments.why: Short intro to Sandi Metz's style; funny, smart, well constructed
comments.text: I'd like to mention that despite OOP being in the title, I thought this book had a lot to teach that isn't specific to OOP architecture or OOP languages. Really, I think the star of the show is TDD and refactoring. For a short intro to Sandi's style and approach, I always recommend this 35min talk: [VIDEO] Aside from any specifically educational content, as a talk it is fantastic - funny, smart, well put together.

comments.author: buren
comments.story: Write code that is easy to delete, not easy to extend
comments.why: Sandi Metz on wrong abstractions versus duplication
comments.text: Couldn't agree more. Sandi Metz has an excellent talk touching on this topic. Developers exaggerated willingness to keep things DRY and elaborates a bit on why: it's one of the easiest things for a not-so-experienced developer to identify and one of the easiest things to teach. Edit: One of the best quotes from that talk is (paraphrased): "The wrong abstraction is a lot more expensive than duplicated code". [VIDEO]

"so before we have written a single program in our language, before we know whether shared behaviour will be important in the applications that will be written in it" read the POODR book, or watch this [VIDEO] it explains how shared behavior works without code duplication and why people tend to mess it up.

comments.author: ValentinTrinque
comments.text: You do have another solution that can lower the amount of conditions: Null Objects. These don’t fit every use cases, but they can allow you to express what’s missing, or not defined, or empty, and avoid nil pointers dereference or conditions to check the state.
